data.text:
The No-Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP) will continue despite suspension of EDSA rehabilitation, the Department of Transportation and the MMDA said.

“NCAP is not just about EDSA… it’s about a more efficient way of enforcing our traffic rules,” says Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon.

Meanwhile, MMDA Head of Special Operations Gabriel Go says there is no reason to stop the enforcement of NCAP, especially since traffic is visibly more orderly now. | via @andietagz & @JervisManahan

data.text:
Investor :
Is there a negative correlation between Indian defence stocks and defence stocks of other countries? Like when HAL or BEL surges, do Lockheed Martin or AVIC lose steam?

Let’s connect the dots. 🧠🧩

🔸Global Defence Stocks Rally Together
In times of geopolitical stress (like the Russia-Ukraine war), defence stocks across the US (Lockheed), UK (BAE), and India (HAL, BDL) surged in sync.
So no this isn't usually a zero-sum game. It’s often a global defence trade.

🔸 India vs. Regional Rivals? Possible.
Your hypothesis makes more sense regionally. If India gains export deals (like HAL-Armenia in 2022), Russia or others may lose market share. But:
Pakistan has no major listed defence firms.
China’s AVIC or Norinco are too state-controlled and opaque for short-term investor sentiment to show.

🔸What Moves Indian Defence Stocks?
Make-in-India localisation✅
Import bans✅
Export push (Armenia, Philippines, Vietnam)✅
Indian defence momentum is often self-driven, unlike globally correlated tech or commodities.

🔸Case Study: India-Pakistan Conflict (April–May 2025)
After weeks of military tension, a ceasefire was reached on May 10.
But the market had already spoken
📈 Indian defence stocks jumped up to 18% in a single day.
📊The Nifty Defence Index (launched Nov 2024) gained 18% in May, double Nifty 50’s 8% return.
Meanwhile, global defence names didn’t see such high-beta moves.

📌Conclusion
No consistent inverse correlation with foreign defence stocks but in micro-events, like India bagging export orders or regional power shifts, there can be localised winners and quiet losers.

It’s not about global competition it’s about who’s winning the next contract.
